findings.where: screen 12 (Mixed: where to fit it), the right answer's motion

findings.where: screen 6 (The supply cable), current arrows against the triangle above them; screen 1 text
findings.what: Screen 1 teaches 'its current leads where the motor's lags, so its vars, Q_C, point down', but screen 6's current arrows on the same picture draw the leading capacitor current pointing up and the lagging motor current below the floor ('down = behind, up = ahead'), the mirror image of the triangle above, and nothing says why the two pictures flip. Add one line that the triangle draws vars, where a coil's point up by convention, while the arrows draw the currents themselves, measured from the voltage, where behind is below, so the capacitor points down in one and up in the other.

findings.where: practice, Rules of thumb (and explain, 'a real motor's vars also change with how hard it is working')
findings.what: 'Keep the capacitor's vars at or below the load's own at its lightest working, since a motor's vars change with its load; more over-corrects.[^8]' is not in the research notes: footnote 8 (Kuphaldt) supports only 'be careful not to over-correct', not the lightest-working rule or the claim that a motor's vars change with load. Source both, or label them as unsourced reading, or cut them to Kuphaldt's caution.

findings.where: screens 5 to 12, the current's moving dots
findings.what: The dots run steadily one way round each loop, and on screens 9 and 10 the spare leading current runs 'the other way' along the cable. That shows AC as a flow travelling round, the very misconception lesson 1 set out to undo ('what alternates is the direction ... not a flow that travels round', notes 5.3), and the 'ignores' line only says the dots do not show charge speed. Either make the dots surge back and forth with the wave, or add a line to the key and to 'ignores' that every current here reverses each half cycle and the dots show only where it runs and how much.

findings.where: screens 1 and 9, the key terms 'power factor correction' and 'over-correction'
findings.what: write() wraps *terms* in <span class="mark">, but the kit styles only the mark element and .term (app/kit/kit.css line 106), so the amber highlight never shows: the 360 px screenshot of screen 1 shows 'power factor correction' in plain text.
